terms.gloss: an idea of what to do, a plan
evidence: Cic. Inv. 1.36: cōnsilium est aliquid faciendī aut nōn faciendī excōgitāta ratiō (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. idea: optimum cōnsilium, a great idea

terms.gloss: it occurs to (someone); I’ve had an idea
terms.grammar: phrase: the person in the dative; the thing as subject, or impersonal with a genitive
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.36.1: sī quid in mentem veniet
Cic. Rosc. Am. 95: venit enim mihi in mentem ōris tuī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: In Cicero the subject is a neuter pronoun or rēs; otherwise the verb is impersonal, with a genitive (Lewis & Short).

Seneca’s loan for Plato’s Idea; Cicero writes the word in Greek (Lewis & Short). It never means a plan or a passing thought, and Morgan–Owens gives idea only in the Platonic sense, marked as a modern word.

phrases.latin: Semper cōnsilium tunc deest, cum opus est maximē.
phrases.english: Good ideas are always missing just when they are most needed.

phrases.latin: Sērō in perīclīs est cōnsilium quaerere.
phrases.english: It is too late to look for a plan in the middle of danger.
